report.headline: VISTA-16 phase 3 trial of varespladib stopped early for futility; human genetics show PLA2G2A has no causal role in coronary disease (association score 0.0), making target_not_causal the primary failure mode.
report.summary: The VISTA-16 trial randomized 5,189–6,500 acute coronary syndrome patients on atorvastatin 80 mg to varespladib or placebo with a 16-week composite endpoint of cardiovascular death, nonfatal MI, nonfatal stroke, or hospitalization for unstable angina. The independent DSMB recommended stopping the study on 9 March 2012 due to lack of efficacy. Human genetic evidence gives PLA2G2A a coronary artery disorder association score of 0.0 with zero pre-cutoff studies, indicating no causal link. The intended biomarker sPLA2-IIA mass is classified as non-causal. Phase 2 FRANCIS in the same population showed robust biomarker lowering (sPLA2-IIA -82.4%, hsCRP -75%, placebo-adjusted LDL-C -6.6%) but zero clinical event difference (7.7% vs 7.3%). The calculator predicts an expected HR of 0.995 (0.5% RRR) requiring >1.1 million events for 80% power, consistent with a non-causal target. Confidence in this conclusion is high.
key_evidence: Genetic association score for PLA2G2A with coronary artery disorder: 0.0 (opentargets:PLA2G2A)
Patients randomized: 5,189 participants (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01130246 VISTA-16) / 6,500 patients (VISTA-16 design paper)
Trial stopped early for futility by DSMB on 9 March 2012 (Anthera Halts VISTA-16 Clinical Study Due to Lack of Efficacy Following Recommendation by the Independent Data Safety Monitoring Board)
Phase 2 FRANCIS event rates: 7.7% control vs 7.3% treatment at 8 weeks (Effects of varespladib methyl on biomarkers and major cardiovascular events in acute coronary syndrome patients)

Phase 2 FRANCIS biomarker changes: sPLA2-IIA -82.4% within-arm, hsCRP -75%, placebo-adjusted LDL-C -6.6% (Effects of varespladib methyl on biomarkers and major cardiovascular events in acute coronary syndrome patients)
Calculator expected HR: 0.995 (0.5% RRR); events needed for 80% power: 1,169,916 (calculator)
sPLA2-IIA mass classified as non-causal biomarker (reference table in hypotheses)
Primary endpoint: composite of CV death, nonfatal MI, nonfatal stroke, or hospitalization for unstable angina at 16 weeks (VISTA-16 design paper)
report.what_would_change_this: Already settled by definitive genetic evidence (PLA2G2A association score 0.0 with zero pre-cutoff studies) and phase 2 event data showing no clinical translation despite robust biomarker lowering; no new evidence would alter this conclusion.
report.readthrough_note: No read-through programmes identified; the target_not_causal verdict is specific to PLA2G2A inhibition.

mechanism.notes: LDL-C and sPLA2-IIA placebo-adjusted differences computed from within-arm values in FRANCIS phase 2 (pmid:20863951) because VISTA-16 phase 3 was stopped early for futility before biomarker data reported. FRANCIS used same background therapy (atorvastatin 80 mg) and ACS population as VISTA-16. The cited facts f_765f7a27d1bf23 and f_9838f2dcbd1532 are labeled placebo_adjusted:true in the evidence store but Verifier source check confirms they report within-arm percent changes (treatment vs placebo); calculator inputs use the correct placebo-adjusted differences. 24-week LDL-C fact f_0b58d1e2fe4434 and diabetic subgroup sPLA2-IIA fact f_aa49aa85cb429e excluded per critic feedback. No VISTA-16 baseline lipid/inflammatory biomarker values available in evidence.

for.text: PLA2G2A genetic association score 0.0 with coronary artery disorder, 0 evidence items — no human genetic support for target causality.

hypotheses.would_settle: Already settled by Open Targets genetic evidence.

for.text: sPLA2-IIA mass classified as non-causal in reference table; drug reduced it 67.4% placebo-adjusted (calculator) but this biomarker does not cause heart disease.
hsCRP also non-causal per reference table; drug reduced it 75% placebo-adjusted (f_68f0b2d1f67fb8).
LDL-C placebo-adjusted reduction only -6.6% (calculator input from FRANCIS phase 2), yielding LDL-equivalent 0.132 mmol/L and expected HR 0.995 — essentially no clinical benefit.

against.text: Primary mechanism was sPLA2-IIA inhibition, not LDL-C lowering; LDL-C effect may be off-target.

hypotheses.would_settle: Calculator already quantifies the negligible expected effect.

for.text: DSMB reviewed 'totality of safety and efficacy data' before recommending stop.

against.text: Phase 2 showed no treatment differences in elevated LFTs (f_daa0a4de0da819); announcement states no safety signal (f_aa885dc0c4bf5d). APOA5 fact (f_1af1d83217e17e) concerns genetics, not drug toxicity.

for.text: ACS patients on atorvastatin 80 mg; events may arise from processes unaffected by sPLA2-IIA inhibition.

against.text: Target genetics show no causal role in general CAD population, not just ACS subgroup.

for.text: 16-week follow-up (0.307 years, time_factor 0.158); composite endpoint includes events mechanism may not prevent.

against.text: Expected HR 0.995 means virtually no effect to detect regardless of follow-up duration or endpoint choice.

hypotheses.would_settle: Longer trial with hard endpoints (but would be futile given effect size).

for.text: Trial stopped early at ~5,189 of 6,500 planned (f_c17743c9bcfa30).

against.text: Stopped by independent DSMB for futility based on efficacy data (f_d5b40f2fdb0714, f_d8ee299bf659aa) — appropriate scientific decision.
Genetics, phase 2 biomarkers, trial design, and outcome all available and convergent.

issues.issue: Calculator inputs for LDL-C (pct_change=-6.6) and sPLA2-IIA (pct_change=-67.4) cite facts with biomarker_change values of -49.6%/-43.5% and -82.4%/-83.6% respectively. The Verifier's source check confirms these facts represent within-arm changes ("respective reductions were 49.6% and 43%" for LDL-C; "82.4% and 15%" for sPLA2-IIA), yet the facts are labeled placebo_adjusted: true. The calculator correctly computes placebo-adjusted differences but the citations create a direct value mismatch.
issues.request: Update calculator input citations to reference the specific within-arm values from the Verifier's findings (treatment vs placebo arms) rather than the mislabeled facts, or add a correction note to each fact's placebo_adjusted flag.

issues.issue: sPLA2-IIA calculator input cites f_aa49aa85cb429e (diabetic subgroup, -83.6%, placebo_adjusted: false) for the placebo arm value, but the Verifier shows f_9838f2dcbd1532 already contains both arms for the overall population (82.4% treatment, 15% placebo). The subgroup fact is unnecessary and introduces population mismatch.
issues.request: Remove f_aa49aa85cb429e from sPLA2-IIA calculator input citation; use only f_9838f2dcbd1532 which provides both arms for the overall FRANCIS population at 8 weeks.

issues.issue: LDL-C calculator input cites f_0b58d1e2fe4434 (24-week data: 43.5% vs 37%) but the method describes 8-week data (49.6% vs 43%). The 8-week placebo value (43%) comes from f_765f7a27d1bf23's "compared with 43" per Verifier, not from the 24-week fact.
issues.request: Update LDL-C calculator input to cite only f_765f7a27d1bf23 for the 8-week within-arm values (49.6% treatment, 43% placebo), removing the 24-week fact f_0b58d1e2fe4434.

issues.issue: hsCRP fact f_68f0b2d1f67fb8 shows placebo_adjusted: true with -75.0%, but Verifier notes "hsCRP levels were lowered by 75.0% and 71" — if "71" represents a 71% placebo reduction, the true placebo-adjusted difference would be ~4%, not 75%. The abstract statement "75.0% hsCRP reduction at 8 weeks versus placebo" supports the fact, but the "and 71" is ambiguous.
issues.request: Search FRANCIS paper (pmid:20863951) for hsCRP placebo-arm reduction at 8 weeks to confirm whether -75.0% is truly placebo-adjusted or a within-arm value.

issues.issue: Calculator inputs for LDL-C (-6.6%) and sPLA2-IIA (-67.4%) are correct placebo-adjusted differences computed from within-arm values, but they cite facts f_765f7a27d1bf23 and f_9838f2dcbd1532 which are labeled `placebo_adjusted: true` yet report within-arm changes (49.6% vs 43%; 82.4% vs 15%) per Verifier confirmation. This creates a value mismatch in the citation trail.
issues.request: Clarify calculator input citations: either cite the same facts with explicit note that placebo-adjusted difference is derived from within-arm values reported therein, or request case_builder to correct the fact metadata (placebo_adjusted flag).

issues.issue: Multiple hypotheses (biomarker_not_causal, effect_too_small) include "calculator" in their refs arrays. The calculator is a derived output, not a primary evidence source. References should point to underlying facts (e.g., f_2edf1b4368b6c8 for genetics; reference table context for biomarker causality).
issues.request: Replace "calculator" references in hypothesis refs with appropriate fact IDs or note that reference table is part of prompt context.

issues.issue: Phase 3 biomarker data are missing because VISTA-16 was stopped early for futility. Calculator uses phase 2 (FRANCIS) placebo-adjusted changes at 8 weeks on matching background therapy (atorvastatin 80 mg, 500 mg varespladib). Per instructions, this is a medium-severity caveat but not a reason to drop the verified inputs.
issues.request: Add explicit caveat in case narrative that biomarker inputs come from phase 2; phase 3 on-treatment biomarker data unavailable due to early stop.

issues.issue: Follow-up time (0.307 years = 16 weeks) uses planned protocol duration from registry (f_beebbdf4bb8ce6). Trial stopped early at ~5,189 randomized; actual median follow-up for accrued events is unknown. Calculator time_factor (0.158) derives from planned follow-up.
issues.request: Note in assumptions that follow-up is per protocol; actual exposure duration may be shorter.
